summary: An announcement that UCSB now ran a server program supporting part of the Remote Job Entry protocol of RFC 407, reachable at a particular socket. It explains the login details and the transmission mode available at the time. More detailed documentation was promised in a later RFC.

eli5.summary: A university announced that its big computer would now accept jobs sent over the network, and told people how to sign in and send them.

subtitle: A January 1973 notice that UCSB now offered a Remote Job Entry server, with login rules and supported commands.

tldr.problem: Users needed to know that UCSB's computer now accepted remote jobs over the network, and how to get in.
tldr.mechanism: A server program resident under socket 5 supports a subset of the Remote Job Entry Protocol of RFC 407, with userid and password login, one transmission mode, and a list of commands.
tldr.outcome: Many features were not yet implemented, and an RFC with more detailed documentation was promised shortly.

today: The unit metadata lists the status of RFC 436 as Unknown. It is a 1973 announcement of a service at one site, and the text does not say how long it ran.

sections.title: The RJS Server at UCSB
sections.content: Mark Krilanovich of UCSB announces that a server program is now resident under socket 5 at UCSB. It supports a subset of the Remote Job Entry Protocol of RFC 407, and the document gives enough information to gain access to and use the more basic functions of UCSB's RJS. More detailed documentation was to follow in another RFC.
sections.eli5: A door to the university computer is now open at a certain number, and this note says how to knock.

sections.title: Logging In
sections.content: Login needs a userid and a password, each one to eight alphameric characters, the first of which must be alphabetic. The userid is for now completely arbitrary. A password is arbitrary the first time it is used with a userid, but later logins with that userid must give the same password. Eventually the UCSB Computer Center would assign userid-password pairs.
sections.eli5: You pick a name and a secret word the first time, and must use the same ones afterwards, like a clubhouse password.

sections.title: What Works and What Does Not
sections.content:
The only transmission mode supported is T (TELNET-like carriage control); any other is treated as T. The only disposition supported is the default transmit-and-discard. The commands ABORT, ALTER, BACK, HOLD, OP RECOVER, RESTART and SKIP are not yet implemented, though some would be soon.

For convenience, INUSER may be used for INID and OUTPATH for OUT. For users of TENEX FTP servers, INACCT and OUTACCT set the account number for file retrieval and storage, and ACCT gets both. Account numbers are one to six alphameric characters, and if none is given the FTP ACCT command is omitted.
sections.eli5: Only the simplest options work so far. Some buttons are still unfinished, and a few extra shortcuts were added for people using certain other systems.
